name: EgoDex
summary: EgoDex is a large egocentric dataset recorded on head-mounted consumer hardware with paired, automatically annotated 3D hand and finger poses across a wide range of everyday dexterous tasks. The annotation is the whole point: raw egocentric video has to pass through a hand-pose estimator before it can supervise anything, and bundling accurate poses at capture time removes the noisiest, most error-prone step in the human-to-robot pipeline.
innovation: Pairing large-scale egocentric video with reliable 3D hand pose captured at recording time rather than estimated afterwards.
Coverage of genuinely dexterous multi-finger tasks, not just parallel-jaw-style pick and place.
matters: Dexterous hand data is the scarcest category in robot learning, and this is one of the largest open sources of it.
limits: Human hand kinematics do not map cleanly onto most robot hands, and there is no force or tactile channel.
lineage: Ego4D-style capture carrying the hand-pose supervision that manipulation actually needs.
